item.description: provisional description: concise description: precise description: formal description: template planning reasoning provisional description: This is my main reasoning about what to do in life ... With the precise name "personal planning stage reasoning", the "personal" is contrasting it with "impersonal planning reasoning" - knowledge of e.g. engineering, medicine, business, etc. Those are "planning reasoning" in the sense that they're optimization problems and the reasoning process is the same. But they're different from my main reasoning about what to do. Because I'm not planning on building a bridge or trying to treat an infection myself. I'm not sure how exactly they help my own planning reasoning at the moment. But I think it could be partly giving me ideas for the planning process. I.e. "personal planning reasoning metacognition". Note that it has alternative names "directed reasoning" and "goal-directed reasoning". This is for contrasting with "undirected reasoning" - thinking I do for curiosity or general knowledge where I'm not trying to answer a single question. concise description: Plans and the reasoning behind them precise description: formal description: planning reasoning provisional description: concise description: General knowledge, plans, and the reasoning behind them precise description: formal description: reasoning provisional description: Reasoning about what to do for certain decisions, both questions and opinions Part of "template planning reasoning" - the planning that applies to most situations, to build on with specific reasoning in "timespan planning reasoning" ... concise description: precise description: formal description: provisional - I'll just start adding things as I think of them then adjust the categories as I go constraint stage template planning reasoning provisional description: concise description: precise description: formal description: other notes (provisional description): Note that this has some "high-level constraints" - that refers to the fact that they're high-level decisions within e.g. the style project.
